Postponement of a simple assessment ends once a final response is given under s31AA(9); a fresh s55(3) application is needed if the customer later appeals.

dcacdb3ba7206ea0.heading: Appeals, Reviews and Tribunals Guidance (ARTG) > ARTG4070 — Scope and limitations of the review

caveats: Where the customer appeals against a closure notice, review scope is limited to the specific conclusions/amendments in that notice; the review cannot alter the scope of the appeal once issued, and HMRC will not give substantive comment on grounds outside that scope.

In exceptional circumstances HMRC may uphold an appealable decision even where the chance of litigation success is less than 50%, provided the decision is defendable and evidence-based.
The review officer has no discretion to depart from current policy/practice without prior approval from relevant policy and technical teams.
If the customer neither accepts the review offer nor notifies the tribunal, the appeal is treated as settled on HMRC's stated view (s.49C(4) TMA 1970).

note.summary: This chunk describes HMRC's internal ARTG guidance on how a customer's appeal proceeds after being sent to HMRC: either via a review (HMRC-offered or customer-requested) or by notification to the tribunal. It sets out timeframes (30 days to accept a review offer or go to tribunal, 45 days for HMRC to conduct a review, 30 days to appeal to tribunal after review conclusion) and the consequence of inaction (appeal treated as settled by agreement under s49C/s49F TMA 1970). It also covers the special rule for Simple Assessments, which carry no right of appeal unless the customer first raises a query under s31AA TMA 1970 within 60 days, and separately describes parallel processes for indirect tax decisions (VATA 1994 s83D) and restoration decisions.
